head_commit.message:
docs: update SECURITY.md with crypto review status and advisory link (#33)

* docs: add automated static analysis results to CRYPTO_REVIEW.md

External review step 7: 'Get one external pair of eyes on the crypto
surface.' We cannot commission an external review in this session, but
we can:

1. Run automated static analysis (bandit) on the crypto surface and
   document the results in CRYPTO_REVIEW.md.
2. Add a CI workflow (.github/workflows/bandit.yml) that runs bandit
   on every PR touching actenon/proof/ or actenon/replay/, so the
   analysis stays current.
3. Be explicit that automated analysis is NOT a substitute for manual
   cryptographic review.

Bandit results: 3 findings, all assessed as false positives:
- B105: hardcoded password (false positive — it's the env var NAME,
  not a password value; the actual secret is explicitly public dev-only)
- B310: url open (false positive — URL is a configured service endpoint,
  not user-controlled)
- B608: SQL injection (false positive — parameterized query with ?
  placeholder; SELECT_FIELDS is a module constant, not user input)

The CRYPTO_REVIEW.md now includes:
- The automated analysis results table (severity, confidence, file:line,
  assessment)
- The command to reproduce
- Limitations of automated analysis (AST-based, can't verify crypto
  correctness, can't detect logic errors, can't verify cross-language
  equivalence)
- An explicit statement that automated analysis is not a substitute
  for manual review

* docs: update SECURITY.md with crypto review status and advisory link

- Made GitHub Security Advisories the preferred reporting channel
  (direct link to the private reporting form).
- Added a 'Cryptographic review status' section that states plainly:
  no external crypto review has been performed; automated analysis
  (bandit) results are in CRYPTO_REVIEW.md; researchers are invited
  to file findings via the reporting channels.
- Points to docs/CRYPTO_REVIEW.md for exact file pointers and
  reviewer questions.

---------

Co-authored-by: Actenon Bot <bot@actenon.org>

head_commit.message:
docs: put guarantee preconditions next to the tagline (#31)

* docs: put guarantee preconditions next to the tagline

External review: 'The tagline is absolute; the guarantee is conditional.
Put the guarantee preconditions next to the tagline, not one click away.'

The kernel README had the preconditions buried at line 416 in the 'What
the Kernel does NOT do' section. This adds the precondition as a
blockquote immediately after the 'one thing' paragraph (the most-read
part of the README), so a developer sees the conditional on the same
screen, not behind a click into SCOPE_AND_GUARANTEES.md.

The precondition states: the edge guarantee holds when the protected
edge is the only path, the backend accepts only brokered credentials,
and the agent has no standing credential. If those conditions are not
met, the Kernel still refuses invalid proofs — but it cannot prevent a
caller that bypasses it from reaching the resource.

* docs: document crypto review needs — no external review yet

External review: 'Get one external pair of eyes on the crypto surface.
AUDIT_RESPONSES.md answering your own diligence questions is good
practice; it isn't a substitute.'

We cannot get external eyes in this session, but we can prepare the
surface so a reviewer can start immediately, and we can be honest that
no external review has been done.

This adds docs/CRYPTO_REVIEW.md which:
- States plainly at the top: 'No external cryptographic review has been
  performed.'
- Lists the 4 surfaces that need external review: canonicalisation,
  replay atomicity, key lifecycle, attestation envelopes.
- For each surface: exact file pointers, spec pointers, conformance
  vector pointers, and the specific questions a reviewer should answer.
- States what this document is NOT (not an audit, not a disclosure,
  not a substitute for adoption-stage diligence).
- Provides instructions for how a security researcher can start a
  review (Security Advisories or email).

Also adds a blockquote to the kernel README's Audit responses section
pointing to CRYPTO_REVIEW.md, so the 'no external review' caveat is
visible on the README, not hidden in a docs/ folder.

---------
